overview: This 618-page file documents Allied oversight of Japanese fishing and whaling after World War II, especially the 1946–47 Antarctic expedition and the contested authorization of a second expedition. Directives, catch statistics, observer reports, diplomatic protests, and policy memoranda trace disputes over food supply, conservation, reparations, fishing limits, and international whaling rules.
interest: The file pairs detailed fleet and catch records with Allied protests, revealing how occupation food policy collided with conservation and diplomacy.
